gen-dafont-klill-fs-fira-sans: Round, open and unfussy, with nothing sharp to snag on. Klill keeps its curve endings well apart, and Fira Sans, with its generous x-height and wide-mouthed s, carries a full page of text along without tiring the eye.
gen-dafont-klill-fs-public-sans: Trustworthy, in a flat, hushed sort of way. Klill does best with a constant line weight and well-spaced curve endings, while Public Sans does best with a hefty lowercase and broad open counters.
gen-dafont-klill-general-sans: Clean and quietly confident, with nothing showy anywhere. Klill's big-bodied lowercase lines up with General Sans, whose steady pressure and smooth bends should make paragraphs of text glide by without a snag.
gen-dafont-klill-switzer: Klill's strokes never swell or thin, from stem to curve. Switzer, a sans-serif with wire-like letterforms and c tips that never touch, matches that openness so closely they look cut from one cloth.
gen-dafont-minecraftia-lora: Lora reads in a bookish, welcoming way, with hairline thinning at the curves and a c that opens broadly. Minecraftia does the playful part, Lora the literary reading.
gen-dafont-ozone-lora: Technical and geometric, with wire-like lines and wide-set curve ends. Lora, with a faint swell in each curve, would carry a long stretch of text in a bookish, literary voice.
gen-dafont-ozone-noto-serif: Ozone draws every counter with a single line weight, crisp and geometric. Noto Serif, with its prominent x-height and subtle stroke modulation, would make a long run of text feel literary and universal.
gen-dafont-pixel-operator-fs-epilogue: Epilogue reads curvy and unclamped, with a generously proportioned lowercase, stubby ascender tips and a wire-like monoline skeleton. Pixel Operator does terminal-style fixed width; Epilogue does soft curves.
gen-dafont-radikal-fs-epilogue: Radikal bends its s curves from wire, never thinning at the spine, with a generous gap after each glyph. Epilogue's open, unclamped curves gently loosen up Radikal's closed letters, and that is the whole charm.
gen-dafont-rounded-elegance-fs-epilogue: Letters in Rounded Elegance sit so close they almost overlap, with wide entrances. Epilogue, a sans-serif with the same wire-like monoline skeleton, keeps that warmth going with looser, curvier shapes.
